summary: Trailing-separator in streamed JSON causes long-tail decode latency spikes
description: Customer reports intermittent high tail latencies (p99 > 10s) for streaming responses when using structured JSON mode. Behavior reproduces when the model emits separators or partial list delimiters across chunk boundaries, causing the server-side JSON streaming decoder to wait for completion before emitting valid JSON tokens to the client. This appears as a long-tail spike (10-30s) and sometimes a server-side request timeout (upstream 504).
impact: Several API calls from Finlytics' production pipelines are hitting p99 latency spikes and occasional 504s during end-of-month reports. Business impact: delayed downstream processing and customer-facing report dashboards lag. Affects enterprise customer on Dedicated capacity—support contract requires timely escalation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use streaming endpoint with structured_output=true and streaming=true
2) Prompt model to emit a JSON array of objects (e.g., 'Return a JSON array of up to 50 transaction summaries')
3) Send request with chunked streaming enabled (curl --no-buffer or websocket streaming client)
4) Observe repeated runs; tail latency spike occurs when model emits separators "," or trailing commas across token boundaries
5) Reproducible in our internal staging with the same prompt when seed/temperature encourages shorter separator tokens
logs: request_id=7f3a1c9b-stream-001 | model=redwood-chat-13b | route=/v1/chat/stream | total_time_ms=17845 | p99: 17845ms | last_chunk_delay_ms=14230
error_sample: upstream=504 | message='deadline exceeded while waiting for final JSON token' | client_ip=54.210.33.12
stacktrace-snippet: streaming-decoder.go: line 312: WaitForCompleteToken() timed out after 12s
investigation: Initial hypothesis: incremental JSON parser blocks waiting for closing structure; when separators are split across chunks the parser's heuristic for emitting partial objects fails and it buffers until a valid complete parse.
Correlation found between requests that include lists/arrays in prompts and higher p99 latencies (ratio ~4x vs non-JSON prompts).
Reproduced locally by lowering model temperature to 0.3 and requesting large arrays: observed identical 'last_chunk' gap where decoder waited for closing bracket that arrived 12-18s later.
Confirmed streaming transport is delivering tokens as expected; root cause is decoder-side parsing logic, not network batching.

Checked related tickets: SUP-24689 and SUP-17821 describe similar JSON streaming buffering but not the trailing-separator case across chunk boundaries. Linked internal follow-up INT-20455 opened to track runtime patch.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer opened this after noticing p99 spikes during end-of-month runs. Provided sample request_id and prompt. Asked for priority escalation.
SRE (Miguel): Collected traces and pprof; confirmed blocking in streaming-decoder.WaitForCompleteToken(). Attached pprof snapshot and preliminary mitigation plan.
Customer (Finlytics SRE): Shared additional logs showing bursts only during large array generation and only for a subset of calls; provided sample prompts and confirmed dedicated capacity.
Eng (Danielle Park): Proposed a short-term mitigation: implement a configurable 'partial-emit-timeout' to flush buffered JSON after X ms of inactivity, with telemetry to track broken JSON emissions.
Support (Aisha): Informed customer of mitigation path and request for permission to enable partial-emit-timeout for their dedicated pool as an opt-in workaround.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: enabled 'partial_json_flush_ms=5000' on Finlytics dedicated pool to reduce tail latency by forcing a flush after 5s of inactivity. This reduced p99 from ~17s to ~3.2s in customer tests but can produce partial JSON which the client must handle. Long-term fix: engineering to implement tolerant incremental JSON parser that recognizes separator tokens across chunk boundaries and emits safe, well-formed partial JSON or synthetic closing tokens until finalization. Follow-up items: INT-20455 (decoder patch), PR linked below. Customer advised to: (a) include explicit closing bracket in prompt when possible, (b) prefer non-streaming responses for large arrays if strict JSON is required, and (c) accept opt-in mitigation for immediate relief.
